case_evidence.description: Frozen public eyetrajectoriespy==1.2.0 src/eyetrajectoriespy/plotting.py::plot_fpca_component_band, matched by optional native strict scientific artist data.

Genuine native matched-bootstrap FPCA component-shape band with original observed grid, same-shape reference components and lower/upper arrays, zero-based fitted FPC index, and exact fitted dimension name (first fitted channel when omitted). Confidence level within (0,1), simultaneous scope family/component. The native domain does not inject or return Python Matplotlib Axes instances.

Original observed time grid and matched/sign-aligned reference FPC array are the source line. Original bootstrap lower/upper component band arrays form fill_between with alpha=.2 and label formatted as %.1f%% simultaneous band, followed by source reference FPC line and legend. Title 'FPCk simultaneous band (familywise/component-wise)' and Time(unit)/FPC loading dimension are source-matched. Committed direct frozen Python 1.2 Matplotlib Line2D and PolyCollection scientific geometry/alpha/label/legend comparisons and tests on genuine native 20-replicate FPCA component-band fits; exact-head success not yet witnessed.

Unsupported native result, invalid/negative/out-of-range component, missing dimension, mismatch of 3D source band arrays, invalid/inverted or nonfinite intervals, invalid confidence level/scope and nonlogical strict flag fail explicitly. Python KeyError/IndexError classes and live Axes behavior differ.

Python returns one Matplotlib Axes with fill_between PolyCollection and reference FPC line. Native R preserves its existing observed-grid mean/interval four-column return by default and emits typed numerical source artist data in strict mode; pixel-perfect polygon rasterization and Python runtime identity are outside scope.

Bootstrap-calibrated simultaneous component-shape uncertainty after sign and component matching to the original full-sample FPCA eigenspace. The reference eigenfunction and source confidence band are not re-estimated by plotting and do not imply pointwise-only coverage.
